summary: Real GBP suspension pain, but the evidence shows agencies paying for rescue after a suspension, not for a prevention vault; the status quo is a free Drive folder and checklist. The matcher needs manual data entry and the buyer is a category, so it falls below the bar.

demand.evidence: RESEARCH.md has only practitioner commentary (SEJ, LocalSearchForum) and rescue pricing (Whitespark $599, Sterling Sky $800). No interviews and no one asking for a vault; prevention spend is unproven.

statusQuo.evidence: BrightLocal checklist plus Drive folders and spreadsheets; a 60-minute upload window is a concrete cost, but the workaround is free and the pain is infrequent.

specificity.evidence: Buyer is 'local-SEO freelancer or small agency, 10-100 listings': a category. Findable on LocalSearchForum and r/LocalSEO, but no named person.

wedge.evidence: MVP is wide (vault, matcher, checklist, packet, score, dashboard). The narrowest sellable piece is the pre-edit risk checklist; the matcher needs manual retyping of document fields.

futureFit.evidence: Depends on a Google-created problem that may fade (one source notes a fix); monitoring incumbents at $19/mo could add a document store.

premises: Agencies will pay recurring fees for prevention, not only rescue (unsupported)
Exact document matching is the main cause of failed appeals (partly supported; Google rarely says which rule was broken)
Agencies will trust a solo developer with business license scans (unverified)
Doing nothing hurts (real but infrequent per client)
alternatives: Minimal: free pre-edit GBP risk checklist page with email capture
Ideal: full vault with GBP API read access and expiry alerts (large, needs OAuth and document security)
Lateral: sell a one-off appeal-packet or template pack at $49-$99 per case
No existing David repo to extend; permitly is a different buyer
wedge: A single page: pick the planned edit, get the risk note and a have-these-ready list, plus a name/address matcher. No accounts, no storage.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel Hobby with pure TypeScript normalizers and a rules table. Proof test: findMismatches returns exactly 1 address mismatch for the Ste 4 vs Ste 5 fixture and 0 for 'Acme Plumbing, LLC' vs 'Acme Plumbing LLC'. This proves the code, not demand. M2 storage of license scans is where cost and liability appear.

risks: Prevention is a hard sell with thin demand evidence
Incumbent monitors add a vault feature
Liability for storing license and bill scans
Small niche; about 35 customers needed for $1k/mo
Manual data entry may kill adoption
killCriteria: Fewer than 5 qualified signups (10+ locations) in 14 days with 50+ qualified visitors; fewer than 3 of 10 interviewed agencies would pay $29/mo; agencies say a free checklist is enough; an incumbent adds document storage.
